# Waypoints

<!-- docs:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Server-managed waypoints with access rules, a Java HUD, and vanilla commands
<!-- docs:end summary -->

<!-- docs:begin reference -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs from package, action, and component docs metadata. Run `pnpm readme`. -->

See the [plugin guide](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/packages/waypoints/docs/) and [API reference](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/api/plugins/waypoints/) on the documentation site.

## Installation

Put `waypoints.wasm` from the plugin's GitHub release in your server's `plugins/` folder and restart. Hot reload cannot ask for permissions, so the first load needs a restart.

## Permissions

<!-- docs:begin permissions -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Pumpkin asks for these on the server console the first time the plugin loads.

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `fs.read.data` | Read the waypoint store from the plugin data folder. |
| `fs.write.data` | Persist waypoint changes in the plugin data folder. |
| `http.outbound` | Check Pumpkin Market for plugin updates. |
<!-- docs:end permissions -->

## Create and use waypoints

Operators can create a waypoint at their exact position with `/wp create "Home Base"`, or provide
absolute coordinates with `/wp create "Home Base" 120.5 64 -30`. Names are unique across worlds.
Use `/wp list` to see enabled waypoints you can access, `/wp info <name>` for details, and
`/wp tp <name>` to teleport yourself. Operators can use `/wp tp <name> @a` to teleport a player selector.

Only server operators can create, edit, enable, disable, grant, or delete waypoints. Administrative
handlers check Pumpkin's operator list even if a command permission was manually granted. Player
grants resolve online names and store UUIDs. Group grants check the permission marker
`Waypoints:group.<slug>`; another permission provider must assign that marker to group members.

The versioned store is `plugins/data/Waypoints/waypoints.json`. If it is malformed or has an
unsupported schema, the plugin preserves it and refuses writes until the issue is corrected. A
successful v1 migration keeps the original bytes in `waypoints.v1.json`.

## Java waypoint HUD

Minecraft Java 26.3 players see each enabled waypoint they can access in the same dimension and
within its optional visibility range. The display shows the waypoint label (or name) in its color
and the rounded distance in meters, with its configured item sprite centered on a line below.
Each player's display packets are private to that player, so
restricted names and personalized distances are not sent to other clients.

The HUD uses client-only TextDisplay packets on a camera-relative plane about three blocks ahead,
updated once per server tick. Within ten blocks, each label eases into a world position two blocks
above its waypoint and stays anchored there within three blocks. Screen direction is eased to reduce
movement jitter; ordinary waypoints use stronger vertical stabilization, while destinations several
blocks above or below the player follow height changes faster. Small stationary camera-position and
yaw changes are also ignored. Other Java protocol versions and Bedrock clients do not receive the
HUD. Icons use vanilla 26.3 atlas textures; block items use a representative model texture, and
custom item IDs require the corresponding `item/<path>` sprite in the client's resource pack.
